absolute_delta_per_subscriber_usd.description: Ground per-subscriber cost minus space per-customer cost (MID), USD/yr.

space_is_cheaper.description: Comparison flag (not an editorial call): space costs less than ground at the mid band in the sparse regime.

cost_to_cost.notes: The same 1.5x margin is applied to both sides, so it cancels and this is a pure cost-structure ratio (the data-center spine), not a market prediction. The space cost is the same on both density regimes (coverage is flat); only the ground denominator differs.

space_priced_cost_per_subscriber_usd.description: Space priced per-customer cost, MID band member (cost x 1.5), USD/yr.

price_to_beat_usd_per_year.description: The founder-set retail reference annualized, the sparse-regime price-to-beat, USD/yr.

undercut_headroom_usd_per_year.description: Price-to-beat minus space priced cost, USD/yr (positive = undercuts).

undercut_passes.description: Market-test flag (not an editorial call): the space priced cost lands under this regime's price-to-beat in the sparse regime.

price_undercut.notes: Sparse: the price-to-beat is the founder-set retail reference (the unserved fringe has no incumbent floor). Dense: the price-to-beat is the incumbent marginal defend floor, far below retail (COMM-096 / COMM-098); the entrant must beat the floor, not the list price.

space_capacity_binds.formula: False for sparse, True for dense (SPECTRUM_spec.md Section 3)
space_capacity_binds.description: Physics flag (not an editorial call, SPECTRUM_spec.md Section 3): the space capacity ceiling binds in the sparse regime (coverage has headroom).

sparse.notes: Space wins on cost in the unserved/remote fringe (the fresh-build ground denominator is far above the modeled space cost) and capacity has headroom (coverage reaches everyone).

space_priced_cost_per_subscriber_usd.description: Space priced per-customer cost, MID band member (cost x 1.5), USD/yr.

price_to_beat_usd_per_year.description: The dense-regime price-to-beat: the incumbent marginal defend cost (COMM-096), the served-market floor the entrant must beat, USD/yr.

undercut_passes.description: Market-test flag (not an editorial call): the space priced cost lands under this regime's price-to-beat in the dense regime.

price_undercut.notes: Sparse: the price-to-beat is the founder-set retail reference (the unserved fringe has no incumbent floor). Dense: the price-to-beat is the incumbent marginal defend floor, far below retail (COMM-096 / COMM-098); the entrant must beat the floor, not the list price.

space_capacity_binds.formula: False for sparse, True for dense (SPECTRUM_spec.md Section 3)
space_capacity_binds.description: Physics flag (not an editorial call, SPECTRUM_spec.md Section 3): the space capacity ceiling binds in the dense regime (a beam cannot densify).

dense.notes: Space loses on cost in the served market (the incumbent marginal defend floor is far below the space cost) and capacity binds (a beam cannot densify below its footprint).

priced_revenue_per_subscriber_usd.formula: cost_annual_per_customer x revenue_multiple  # 1.5x for a 33.3% regular margin
priced_revenue_per_subscriber_usd.description: The space priced per-customer revenue, MID band member (cost x 1.5), USD/yr.

arpu_collectable_revenue_usd.description: The collectable revenue ceiling (ARPU x 12 x operator-share), USD/yr.

priced_below_collectable.description: Flag: the priced revenue is at or below the ARPU-collectable ceiling.

priced_below_retail.description: Flag: the priced revenue is at or below the retail reference.

collectable_win.description: Flag: the priced revenue is at or below BOTH the ARPU-collectable ceiling and the retail reference (the collectable-win gate).

revenue_ceiling.notes: The priced revenue is the space per-customer cost x 1.5. The ceilings are the retail reference and ARPU x operator-share. A collectable win needs the priced cost under both ceilings (plan Section 0.9, the revenue-ceiling gate).

bottom_up_chain_cost_usd_per_sub_year.description: The bottom-up space per-customer cost (the chain figure), MID member, USD/yr.

disclosed_starlink_floor_usd_per_sub_yea.description: The disclosed all-in Starlink floor, USD/yr (a disclosed-financials reference, not a Rocket Lab figure).

chain_below_disclosed_floor.description: Flag (reported only): the bottom-up chain figure is below the disclosed Starlink floor. Being below is NOT claimed as a win.

starlink_floor.honesty_note: Both the bottom-up space chain figure and the disclosed all-in Starlink floor are shown and labeled. The model never claims the bottom-up chain beats the disclosed all-in Starlink number; being below the disclosed floor is reported, not asserted as a win.

warnings.what_tested: Comparison interpretation and the sparse-vs-dense split.
warnings.expected_condition: The comparison is a per-density MAP (the two ratios point in opposite directions by design), the retail reference is founder-set, and the editorial judgement is hand-written in Phase 6.
warnings.observed_result: Order-of-magnitude cost screen reported per density regime; the sparse-vs-dense crossover is a zone, not a sharp point (about the dense-suburban fringe, COMM-103); the editorial judgement is hand-written in Phase 6, not asserted here.
warnings.remediation_hint: Read the sparse and dense regimes separately; do not blend them into a single comms-wide ratio.
